descRo: The nearest major spiral galaxy to the Milky Way, visible to the naked eye as a soft elliptical glow.
name: Andromeda Galaxy

descRo: The most spectacular stellar nursery in the night sky, visible beneath Orion's Belt.
name: Orion Nebula

descRo: The famous open star cluster in Taurus, consisting of over 1,000 young stars wrapped in blue reflection nebulosity.
name: Pleiades (Seven Sisters)

descRo: The brightest globular cluster in the northern hemisphere, containing over 300,000 ancient stars.
name: Great Hercules Cluster

descRo: Spectacular expanding shell of ionized gas expelled by a dying red giant star in Lyra.
name: Ring Nebula

descRo: Giant interstellar cloud of ionized gas in the Sagittarius arm of the Milky Way.
name: Lagoon Nebula

descRo: Grand-design spiral galaxy with prominent arms, interacting gravitationally with a companion dwarf galaxy.
name: Whirlpool Galaxy

descRo: Lenticular galaxy with a bright nucleus and a striking absorption dust lane reminiscent of a sombrero hat.
name: Sombrero Galaxy

descRo: Luminous open star cluster in the tail of Scorpius, documented by ancient astronomer Ptolemy in 130 AD.
name: Ptolemy Cluster

descRo: The first planetary nebula ever discovered (by Charles Messier in 1764), featuring an iconic hourglass shape.
name: Dumbbell Nebula
